area: tax: Sales tax decisions (H8-H13 Hasnain defaults + owner delivery-fee decision): delivery fee GST, kept no-show deposits, gift-card breakage, card MDR at payout, input tax by authority + withholding on bills/OpEx (CapEx through the FA area), customer sales-tax withholding
summary:
When this is built:

1) DELIVERY FEE (owner 2026-10-13 + H9 'brand'). The zone fee stays the fee before tax. lib/pricing.ts priceOrder adds GST on top of it, at the order's standard tender rate (cash 15%, card/Raast/online 8%), rounded on its own: deliveryFeeTaxCents = round(fee x rate / 100). Order.taxCents = GST on the food + GST on the fee. The total = food + food GST - discount + fee + fee GST + service charge. Service charge and tip % never include the fee or its GST. Two new INT4 columns, Order.deliveryFeeCents and Order.deliveryFeeTaxCents, are written by ingestOrder from the price, so every channel stores what it charged.
 - Storefront quote and checkout return the split: itemTaxCents, deliveryFeeTaxCents, taxCents.
 - The checkout page and the mobile app show one GST row (with 'incl. PKR x on delivery') and a Delivery row. The mobile app stops computing a local 17%; it reads GET /storefront/quote and sends the real checkout body.
 - The receipt (HTML and JSON), the tablet printer, the admin order page and the TaxInvoice show the fee. Its GST sits inside the GST row, so the printed rows add up to the total.
 - Rider cash-to-collect is the pending payment, so it already includes the fee and its GST (tested, no code change).
 - WhatsApp ordering and group orders are pickup / till only: no fee, no change (tested).
 - Ledger: the fee leaves brand revenue and goes to a new 4110 Delivery Fee Income. order.complete and shift.close credit it, tagged with the brand. Refunds debit their share of it (refundShareOf).
 - Fiscal payload: the fee becomes a taxed line (itemCode DELIVERY-CHARGE, the order's rate, its stored GST). Discount covers the food first, then this line, then billDiscount. totals.deliveryChargeCents is 0 for new orders and keeps the untaxed remainder rule only for legacy orders. The vendor contract (docs/pos-connector-api.md) gets a dated, backward-compatible note. Nothing new reaches the POS outside completeOrder.
 - Sales-tax return: delivery charges become their own supply rows per authority and rate. Taxable sales include 4110 per brand.

2) KEPT NO-SHOW DEPOSIT (H10 'taxable'). reservations/depositCapture.ts (the TODO(G9) seam) keeps its sourceType, claim and idempotency. It now books Dr 1030 / Cr the brand's revenue account (tax-exclusive part) / Cr the brand's output-tax account, with tax = round(D x taxRateCard / (100 + taxRateCard)), because the hold is card-gateway money. Every line is tagged with the brand. No fiscal document is created (it is not an order). The return shows these as 'No-show deposits kept' rows per authority, so they are declared.

3) GIFT-CARD BREAKAGE (H11 'breakage'). In the daily expiry sweep (giftCards/books.ts expireDueGiftCards, the TODO(G10) seam), each card expires in one row-locked transaction:
 - its balance goes to 0 and GiftCard.breakageCents records it;
 - 'giftcard.expire:<card>[@n]' posts Dr 2080 / Cr 4200 for a sold card (other income, no sales tax), or Cr 6060 for a promotional card.
 - Value a refund later puts back on an expired card is swept as '@n'.
 - Voiding a SOLD card as 'forfeit' is now allowed (admin/owner only) and posts Dr 2080 / Cr 4200.
 - A refused expiry is flagged posting_failed and gets a re-poster.

4) CARD MDR AT PAYOUT (H12 'payout'). The bank-statement import gets a card-payout pass beside the Raast pass (reconciliation/cardPayouts.ts).
 - Company settings (OperationsConfig.cardSettlement): payout bank, MDR, tax on the fee, lag days, tolerance, start day.
 - For each credit on the payout bank, the pass looks for runs of 1-3 unsettled PKT days of card money in 1030.
 - When EXACTLY ONE run fits net = gross x (1 - mdr x (1 + feeTax)) within tolerance, it posts 'card.settlement:<line>': Dr payout bank net / Dr 6080 fee (the tax on the fee included, as a cost) / Cr 1030 gross. The line is marked matched, and the days are claimed once each (CardSettlement / CardSettlementDay, tenant-scoped, RLS).
 - Otherwise the line stays unmatched with suggestions. Finance can confirm a suggestion (fee capped). Approvers can undo.
 - Period close warns (409 CARD_UNSETTLED) on stale unsettled card days.

5) INPUT TAX BY AUTHORITY + WITHHOLDING (H8 'same', H28 'yes').
 - New accounting/taxAuthorities.ts is the one authority table, with inputTaxCodeFor (fbr 1320, pra 1321, srb 1322, kpra 1323, bra 1324).
 - Supplier bills carry taxAuthority (default supplier.defaultTaxAuthority, else fbr). postSupplierBill debits that authority's input account. Credit notes already follow the bill's own input code.
 - Supplier gains filer status, exemption certificate (number, valid until), default tax authority and default WHT section.
 - New lib/withholding.ts is the one WHT resolver. Rates per section (153(1)(a), 153(1)(b), 153(1)(c), 155) x filer / non-filer, per company in OperationsConfig.withholdingRates. The old single withholdingTaxPct is the 153(1)(a) filer default, behind the existing withholdingTaxEnabled switch.
 - Bills use the resolver (snapshot of section and rate on the bill).
 - OpEx lines can name their vendor (a Supplier of the company), a WHT section and a usual tax authority.
 - OpEx payments take the invoice amount, the input sales tax and its authority. The server computes WHT and cash = invoice - WHT, and the existing 'opex.payment' posting (syncSourcePosting) becomes Dr 6xxx (invoice - input tax) / Dr 132x input tax / Cr bank cash / Cr 2040 WHT.
 - CapEx WHT and input tax are built by the FA/CapEx area on the same resolver and authority helpers (a contract, not a second copy).
 - A withholding register (bills, OpEx, CapEx) with CSV is added for the CA's s.165 statement. Rates are editable by admin / finance.
 - The return's input rows now hold real 1321-1324 figures.

6) CUSTOMER SALES-TAX WITHHOLDING (H13 'separate'). POST /accounting/receivables/:id/withholding takes kind 'sales_tax':
 - Dr 1335 / Cr 1110, 'receivable.stwh:<payment>', in the invoice's company.
 - The authority is the output account the invoice's issue entry credited.
 - Capped at the invoice's tax less credited tax less what is already withheld. Reversible through the existing reverse route.
 - The return shows 'Withheld by customers' per authority and deducts it from that authority's net payable.
 - Recording a tax payment can set it off (Cr 1335, capped per authority under a lock).

No new module id. Every route sits under an existing gate (storefront, accounting, reconciliation, opex/capital, procurement, gift_cards). Every new table carries tenantId, has RLS and per-company unique keys. Every posting takes its company from the source document, runs inside the document's transaction and is idempotent on sourceType:sourceId. Every new route ships with two-company tests.

shift.close:<shiftId> (EXISTING): per brand, Cr 4110 Σ deliveryFeeCents (till orders carry 0 today, but the formula is shared). Company = shift's company, as now.

order.refund:<paymentId> / order.refund_wallet:<orderId> / order.refund_giftcard:<redemptionId> (EXISTING): refundShareOf takes the cumulative pro-rata share of deliveryFeeCents -> Dr 4110 (conceptId). card.settlement:<statementLineId>[@n] (NEW): Dr <import.accountCode, the payout bank's chart code> net (memo 'CARD PAYOUT <dayFrom>–<dayTo>') / Dr 6080 gross - net (fee incl. the tax on it, H12) / Cr 1030 gross. backend/src/lib/pricing.ts:

data_migration:
Forward-only. Nothing destructive. Every step is safe to re-run.
- Orders: NO backfill of deliveryFeeCents/deliveryFeeTaxCents. Legacy delivery orders keep 0. Their fee stays where it was booked (brand revenue), the fiscal payload's legacy remainder rule (untaxed deliveryChargeCents) keeps building their documents and refunds, and refunds mirror their sale (no 4110 share). This is deliberate: backfilling would make refunds debit 4110 for fees the sale never credited there. Orders in flight at deploy (priced before) complete exactly as priced.
- Chart: ensureChartOfAccounts adds 4110, 4200 and 1335 at boot for every company (only missing codes, idempotent). /health then sees the new required 4110/4200.
- Gift cards: cards already 'expired' at deploy with balance > 0 get their breakage on the first 00:10 PKT sweep, dated that day (the original expiry month may be closed). The sweep is idempotent per card through the 'giftcard.expire:<id>' reference under the row lock, so re-runs post nothing new.
- No-show deposits captured before deploy (Cr 4100, no tax) stay as booked. The return shows only the new taxed captures as deposit rows. The CA may adjust the old ones by hand; the TAX_SETUP.md note says so.
- SupplierBill.taxAuthority defaults to 'fbr', matching every existing 1320 posting. Supplier.filerStatus defaults to 'unknown' (filer rate plus a 'Check ATL' warning). OpexPayment tax/WHT columns default to 0, so existing OpEx entries are unchanged and only re-post when edited.
- OperationsConfig.withholdingRates = null means defaults, with the existing withholdingTaxPct as the 153(1)(a) filer rate, so bills withhold exactly as today until finance edits rates. cardSettlement = null means card payouts are off until finance saves the settings; startDay = the save day, so days cleared earlier by manual splits are never auto-matched.
- If the migration fails on deploy: it is additive, so prisma migrate resolve --rolled-back 20261014090000_tax_decisions and redeploy. No BIGINT widening is involved.
assumptions: H9 'brand': the delivery fee GST uses the order's standard tender rate (Order.taxRatePct: 15% cash / 8% card, Raast, online, wallet) even when the basket is zero-rated or exempt. It is rounded on its own, round(fee × rate / 100), and stored as deliveryFeeTaxCents.
Zone fees (DeliveryZone.feeCents) are fees BEFORE GST. The customer pays fee + GST on top (owner: 'customer pays more'). A free-delivery zone or tier perk means fee 0 and tax 0.
Service charge and the tip % never include the delivery fee or its GST (the existing pricing rule extended).
Discounts or loyalty beyond the food value cover the delivery line before becoming billDiscount in the fiscal payload. The ledger books discounts to 7010 as today, without a food/fee split.

Fiscal contract: the fee is a normal taxed line with itemCode 'DELIVERY-CHARGE' (FBR reference ItemCode 'DELIVERY', PCT 9963.1100 until the vendor or CA says otherwise). version stays 1, and the change is noted in docs/pos-connector-api.md.

Single GST row on every customer surface (checkout, mobile, receipt, tablet, admin order page). It shows taxCents including the delivery GST, with a 'incl. PKR x on delivery' hint, plus a separate Delivery row, so the rows add up.
WhatsApp ordering and group orders stay pickup / till only. They carry no delivery fee and need no code change (covered by tests).
Mobile: adding expo-location (an exact SDK-52-compatible version) is acceptable for the app, which has not shipped. Without location permission, mobile offers pickup only.

H10: a kept deposit is card-gateway money (the hold debits 1030), so it is taxed at the brand's card rate with the tax inside, and credited to the brand's revenue account. No fiscal document is created (not an order, and the POS contract has no non-order document). It is declared through the return's deposit rows.

H11: breakage is taken at expiry (balance to 0, recorded in breakageCents), dated the sweep day. Promotional cards return to 6060. Forfeiting a SOLD card is income recognition without a refund, so it is limited to APPROVERS (admin, owner). There is no 'reinstate expired card' route; goodwill is a new promotional card.

H12: the whole difference between gross and net (MDR plus the tax on it) is booked to 6080. feeTaxBps is used only to predict the payout and to show the split. One payout bank per company. A day of card money is settled by exactly one payout (Keenu settles per day); split-merchant cases use the existing APPROVERS adjustment. Card gross per PKT day comes from the 1030 ledger (sale, gift-card and deposit entries), not TerminalCharge, so settlement clears exactly what the books hold.

Card settlement settings live in OperationsConfig.cardSettlement (the company finance-rules singleton). They are edited by finance on the reconciliation page, not in the IT-owned connector settings (the frozen TerminalSettings contract stays untouched).

H8 'same': input tax is recorded under the authority that charged it and set off only against that authority's output (the existing return rule). A cross-authority set-off stays a manual JE signed by the CA.
WHT base = the invoice value excluding the sales tax charged on it (bills: subtotal, as today; OpEx: invoice - input tax). The CA confirms.

The WHT rate table defaults (153(1)(a) 5%/10%, 153(1)(b) 9%/18%, 153(1)(c) 7%/14%, s.155 15%/30%, as filer/non-filer) are placeholders Hasnain confirms before switching withholding on for OpEx. All WHT (bills, OpEx, CapEx) obeys the existing company switch withholdingTaxEnabled. With no stored table, today's single % is the 153(1)(a) filer rate, so bills are unchanged.
Filer status 'unknown' withholds at the FILER rate and raises a 'Check ATL status' warning. This keeps today's bill behaviour; Hasnain may tighten it to the non-filer rate later.

OpEx WHT needs the line to name its vendor as a Supplier of the same company. Supplier is the one vendor master (landlords and service vendors become Suppliers; a category filter keeps procurement lists usable). There is no second vendor table and no vendor-create endpoint outside Procurement.

CapEx input tax and WHT (H28) are built by the FA/CapEx area on lib/withholding.ts and accounting/taxAuthorities.ts (the earlier FA design already owns capexPosting.ts and the CapEx columns). This area does not edit capexPosting.ts.

H13 'separate': sales tax withheld by a client is counted in ReceivableInvoice.whtCents (the one 'withheld' figure in balanceOf), told apart by ReceivablePayment.method 'stwh' and taxAuthority. Its authority is the output account the invoice's issue entry credited.
Petty-cash spends and cash-request receipts book gross in this build, with no input tax or WHT (another area builds those flows).
No new module id: every new route falls under an existing gated prefix, so workspaces.ts, moduleAccess.ts and moduleCatalog.ts are unchanged.
4110 and 4200 are required chart codes. 1335 is not (it is posted on demand and refused clearly if missing).
risks: Customer price rise on delivery orders: a basket quoted just before deploy is re-priced at checkout. The page re-fetches the quote, but a customer mid-checkout may see the total change once. Deploy in a quiet hour.

The fiscal POS vendor may reject a non-menu 'DELIVERY-CHARGE' line, or map PCT codes differently. Confirm with the vendor before go-live; a rejected document is held as fiscal_failed and alerted (totals stay consistent), never lost.
The kept-deposit output tax and receivable (B2B) output are not filed through the fiscal POS. Finance must declare them from the return's rows; this is documented in TAX_SETUP.md.

Shared-file contention: orderPosting.ts, salesTaxReturn.ts, supplierPosting.ts, procurement/*, receivables/routes.ts, accounting/routes.ts (period close), backfillOrders.ts, the procurement page, the receivables page and the orders/[id] page are also touched by other wave-B areas (food cost/GRNI, FA/CapEx, on-account, bad debt, year-end, COD overrides). The orchestrator must merge them in order and re-run the full suite.

Coordination gap: if the FA/CapEx area does not deliver CapEx WHT and input tax this wave, H28 is only half built. The orchestrator must check that its syncCapexPaymentPosting uses computeWithholding / inputTaxCodeFor and adds no second rate table.

Card auto-match false positives: two business days with near-identical gross could pair with the wrong payout. Mitigations: the exactly-one-fit rule across all candidate runs and lines, a tight tolerance, startDay, the CardSettlementDay unique key, and the APPROVERS undo route.

Manual Keenu splits booked before deploy (reconciliation.adjustment on 1030) cannot be traced to days. startDay excludes earlier days, but 1030 ageing before startDay still needs a one-off manual clear by finance.

WHT rate defaults may be legally wrong for the current Finance Act (rates change each July). Withholding on OpEx stays behind the existing switch, and the rates are editable; Hasnain must confirm them before enabling.
Breakage for cards that expired before deploy lands in the deploy month's P&L (other income) rather than the month each card expired.
Supplier lists gain landlords and service vendors (procurement noise). The supplier category filter is the mitigation.
Installed tablet builds without the new Delivery print line print totals that do not visibly add up on delivery receipts until the tablet updates (rarely used for delivery orders).
BIGINT rule: cardDayGross uses raw SQL. Sums must be cast ::bigint and passed through toCents, or JSON gets strings or bigints (CLAUDE.md BOOKS-06).
